channelTitle: December 5 in the Alps - the night Santa's shadow comes out - Part 1
hook: In Alpine villages, good kids get St. Nicholas - but the naughty ones get a visit from something with horns, chains, and a basket on its back.
storyParts: Every December fifth in the mountains of Austria and Bavaria, St. Nicholas comes to reward good children - but he does not travel alone. Walking beside him is something older and far less friendly.

His name is Krampus - a half-goat, half-demon figure covered in dark fur, with curling horns, a long red tongue, and chains he drags behind him. On his back he carries a birch switch - and an empty basket.

The old rule was simple: St. Nicholas left sweets and oranges for children who behaved, while Krampus swatted the ones who did not - and legend said the very worst went into the basket and down to the underworld.

Here is the strange part - Krampus is likely older than Christmas itself. Historians trace him to pre-Christian mountain spirits of the harsh Alpine winter, which means the church spent centuries trying to stamp him out.
They never managed it. Villages kept the custom quietly for hundreds of years - until the early nineteen hundreds, when Krampus suddenly came roaring back in a way nobody expected.
cta: How Krampus went from banned to a street festival of thousands of horned runners - Part 2 in the Krampus Night playlist.
